catfish.name: Catfish

sections.whatItOffers: Catfish (cooked): 3 oz cooked gives about 122 calories, with vitamin B12 (about 98%), potassium (about 12%) and 15.6 g of protein. Percentages are of the NIH reference intake for adult women.
sections.howToEatIt: Bake, grill or pan-fry fillets; a light coating of cornmeal or spices works well.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for catfish.

octopus.name: Octopus

sections.whatItOffers: Octopus (cooked): 3 oz cooked gives about 139 calories, with vitamin B12 (about 1275%), iron (about 45%), zinc (about 36%), 25.3 g of protein and 0.27 g of omega-3 (EPA + DHA). Percentages are of the NIH reference intake for adult women.
sections.howToEatIt: Simmer slowly until tender, then slice for salads or grill briefly.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for octopus. Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS); this serving has about 8.1 mg.

smoked-salmon.name: Smoked salmon

sections.whatItOffers: Smoked salmon: 2 oz gives about 67 calories, with vitamin B12 (about 77%), 10.4 g of protein and 0.26 g of omega-3 (EPA + DHA). Percentages are of the NIH reference intake for adult women.
sections.howToEatIt: Serve on toast or bagels, with eggs, or in salads and pasta.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for smoked salmon.
